Hi Ben — thanks for the recap and the doc. Quick answers from AppSec: 

- Yes, Payly considers cardholder name and email as PII. PAN (card number) is obviously never stored.
- For logs, we prefer redacted bodies (no raw request/response payloads) and hashed identifiers for traceability. Trace IDs + minimal routing headers are sufficient for incident triage.
- Retention: standard is 90 days for telemetry; 1 year for audit logs (we can be flexible for mobile/web request logs but not audit trails).

We'd appreciate a sample config showing how Redwood would strip or mask the following fields: cardholder_name, email, ip_address, and any Authorization header values. Also include an example of how you'd retain a hashed user_id versus cleartext.

Monday 11am PST works for a short meeting with our AppSec lead (I'll send a calendar invite). Please loop in whoever owns security config on your side.

Sara
Sara Lin
Director, Security & Risk — Payly

Ben / Lauren — high level plan below (we can expand into an internal runbook before Monday):

1) Redaction profile (config-first)
 - request_body: redact keys ["cardholder_name", "email", "ssn"]; replace values with "<REDACTED>"
 - response_body: redact all PII-related keys by default; allow explicit allowlist for non-PII fields
 - headers: strip Authorization entirely from persisted logs; keep hashed(trace_id) and routing headers (x-request-id, x-service)
 - ip_address: store as truncated /24 for IPv4 (e.g., 203.0.113.0/24) unless full IP is required for fraud investigations (special-case with audit)

2) Hashing scheme
 - use HMAC-SHA256 with customer-provided salt (option) or per-tenant salt managed by Redwood KMS; store only the hex digest in logs to preserve linkability without PII

3) Retention & access
 - telemetry: default 90 days; audit logs retention configurable up to 1 year with stronger access controls and separate KMS-protected envelope
 - read access restricted to named roles; exports require signed request and an approval workflow

4) Evidence pack for AppSec
 - we can deliver: (a) sample log lines showing masked values, (b) a short test harness that posts synthetic requests and demonstrates redaction, (c) an exclusion policy for trace/debug mode (disabled by default)

I'll prepare the config snippet and a couple of sample log lines (one request, one audit) and drop into the Drive link.

—Vivek
